subject: Conditional retainer vs consumption: fallback burn & rollover credits
thread_summary: Negotiation about whether SignalShift should take a conditional retainer (commit) vs pure consumption pricing. Customer asks for a fallback 'burn' policy for unused committed dollars and a 6-month rollover credit option. Sales team evaluates concessions and proposes a limited rollover + phased retainer with technical handoff credit.
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@signalshift.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: SignalShift Procurement <procurement@signalshift.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial terms question on commercial structure

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We like Redwood's latency profile, but our Finance team is pushing back on large upfront retainer commitments. They asked whether you can offer a hybrid — a smaller retainer that gives us lower unit pricing, but with a fallback "burn" mechanism for unused committed dollars and a limited rollover window (we were thinking 3-6 months).

Specifically: can you: 1) shrink the minimum retainer to $25k/month for the first six months, 2) allow 50% of unused committed dollars to roll over for up to 6 months, and 3) define a burn policy if we don't hit thresholds?

Can you confirm what concessions you can make (credits, onboarding waivers, technical handoff support)? We're on a tight procurement timeline (closing by the end of September).

Appreciate a quick outline — procurement copied.

Best,
Amy
Amy Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
SignalShift

Attachment: SS_requirements_summary.pdf (stated - included separately)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: initial terms question on commercial structure

Hi Amy — thanks, and great questions. High level: we can do a hybrid but need to balance unit economics and capacity planning.

Quick answers up front:
- We can propose a $25k/month conditional retainer for a 6-month pilot, with a tiered per-token price that kicks in at commit levels.
- For unused committed dollars, we can offer a 50% rollover for up to 3 months (6 months is aggressive given forecasting).
- Burn policy: after the 3-month rollover window, remaining committed dollars are forfeited unless you convert to a longer-term committed contract.

I'll loop in Jonas and Grace to confirm what we can attach as onboarding credits and SOW support. If timeline is end of September, we should finalize a short side-letter capturing the pilot terms.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal check on onboarding credits and SOW scope (Jonas)
2) Draft short commercial side-letter (Grace)
3) Share redlined side-letter for SignalShift legal by Wed 9/17

I can do a 30-min call today if helpful.

Thanks,
Irene

Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: internal - SignalShift ask (retainer/rollover/burn)

Irene / Grace — quick internal note before we respond more formally to Amy:

- 25k/month retainer is OK for a 6-month pilot, but this only covers baseline warm-start capacity. If their sustained usage exceeds the commit by >30% we should require a run-rate re-eval and provide cost protections.
- Rollover at 50% is acceptable but limit to 3 months. Rationale: KV/cache and reserved GPU slots are provisioned per commit; longer rollovers penalize other customers and the unit economics suffer.
- Burn policy suggestion: staged burn — first 3 months: full rollover at 50% credit; months 4-6: 25% rollover; month 7+: forfeiture unless converted. This phased approach is easier to sell to Finance and reduces our risk.
- Credits: recommend 30k onboarding credit for technical handoff (1x) applied in month 1, contingent on completing the integration checkpoints in the SOW.

If Grace can draft the side-letter with these points, I'll sign off.

-Jonas
VP, Commercial Strategy

- Monthly retainer: $25,000 prepaid each month to secure baseline capacity and priority routing
- Unit pricing: two-tier per-token pricing (below threshold / above threshold) with thresholds tied to commit level
- Rollover: 50% of unused commit credited for up to 3 months after month-end; 25% credit in months 4-6; remainder forfeited thereafter

- Early termination / conversion: if SignalShift converts to a 12-month commit within the pilot, all forfeited credits are reinstated and applied retroactively
- SLA & fallbacks: include a fallback to a compatible smaller model variant if capacity constrained, with service credits for missed SLOs

I'll assemble the draft side-letter and attach the SOW checklist.
